latin: Processus spiritus sancti temporalis attenditur secundum dona gratiae gratum facientia.
translation: The temporal procession of the Holy Spirit is measured according to the gifts of sanctifying grace.
translation_note: 'dona gratiae gratum facientia', the gifts of grace that make [the recipient] pleasing [to God], is Thomas's own phrase for sanctifying grace, per Edelheit's citation of the parallel Thomistic text (edelheit2022:10301).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch2, from Latin at farmer1998:11312

sources.text: Thomas Aquinas, Summa theologiae, 1, question 43, article 3
sources.pico_relation: Edelheit identifies this article, on whether invisible divine mission occurs only through the gift of grace, as the thesis's source

doctrine: The thesis holds that the Holy Spirit's temporal procession is measured by the gifts of sanctifying grace (farmer1998:11312). Edelheit reports that in thesis 2 the temporal procession of the Holy Spirit is extended according to the gifts of grace granted to the one worthy of grace, and finds this in Thomas's Summa theologiae, 1, question 43, article 3 (edelheit2022:10271). Farmer's note places theses 2.2-9 together as concerning various sides of the problem of divine omnipotence and free will (farmer1998:11348).
historiography: Edelheit (2022) quotes Pico's Latin as printed at page 220 of the 900 Theses alongside Thomas's own wording from the Summa, 1, question 43, article 3 (edelheit2022:10301).

quotations.text: In thesis 2 we find that the temporal procession of the Holy Spirit is extended according to the gifts of grace granted to the one worthy of grace.

not_established: The large cross-reference network Farmer records for this thesis (25 entries) is not individually discussed in the excerpts consulted beyond the bare list of thesis numbers.
